P.note: A perspective blue-acrylic disc with clouds caught inside it, hyperreal grass and a bright blown-out horizon, superbly legible and accessible, though the navy type and softer sky read slightly more corporate than Frutiger Aero.

Q.note: A fully committed Frutiger Aero look with translucent vinyl and gel buttons, but the chips, trust badge, bubbles, sparkles and an outlined chromatic-fringe headline make it busy, and body overflow:hidden blocks page scroll.

R.note: A record half inside a tinted PVC sleeve, multiply-blended so the color truly reads as inside the material, though the large blue sleeve slab and the flat pale left hill weigh the composition down.

S.note: Clean, legible and well engineered, with a nice lens label that shows the landscape upside down, but the soft sky and conventional layout feel less charged and less Y2K than the brief asks for.

T.note: The best expression of color inside the material: grass and clouds show through a transparent disc and an overlapping PVC sleeve under a saturated sky with a blown-out sun, kept restrained and legible.

U.note: The most maximal Y2K take, with a lime gel CTA, large bubbles, sparkles, grass chips and a vignette, but the disc reads as a painted gradient and the whole scene tips into clutter and pastiche.
